issues.legal_issue: An acquisition notification’s omission of a particular scheme purpose does not invalidate the acquisition where affected owners knew of that purpose and had an effective opportunity to object to it.
material_facts: The acquisition notifications and notice did not disclose that land was also being acquired for shopping sites.
The scheme included shopping sites, and the owners knew this when they filed objections.
The owners objected to the shopping-site component, including by challenging the shops and seeking the relevant land or a shop site.
issues.conclusion: The omission caused no prejudice because the owners knew of and objected to the shopping-site purpose; the challenge to the notifications on that ground failed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 16 and 17 of the City of Mysore Improvement Act, 1903, the scheme is notified and affected persons may object before it is submitted for government approval. An omission in the notification is not a basis to invalidate the acquisition where it caused no prejudice to the affected owners’ opportunity to make representations.

rule.if: acquisition_scheme_challenge and notification_omitted_scheme_purpose and affected_owners_knew_purpose and affected_owners_objected_to_purpose

predicates.acquisition_scheme_challenge: The proceeding challenged an acquisition made under an improvement scheme.
predicates.notification_omitted_scheme_purpose: The notification did not disclose one of the purposes included in the scheme.
predicates.affected_owners_knew_purpose: The affected owners knew of the omitted purpose when they made their representations.
predicates.affected_owners_objected_to_purpose: The affected owners made representations opposing the omitted purpose.

issues.definition: When an acquisition scheme is challenged, omission of a scheme purpose from the notification does not invalidate the acquisition if the affected owners knew of and objected to that purpose.

issues.legal_issue: Land may be acquired under an improvement scheme for shopping sites intended for the construction of shops.
material_facts: The improvement scheme provided for shopping sites.
The sites were intended for shops.
The scheme concerned the improvement or development of the area.
issues.conclusion: The Board had authority to acquire land for the shopping sites.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15(1)(b) of the City of Mysore Improvement Act, 1903 permits an improvement scheme to provide for the construction of buildings, which includes shops. Section 15(2)(d) permits provision for the establishment or construction of markets; constructing shops amounts in effect to constructing a market.

predicates.improvement_scheme_case: The acquisition was undertaken as part of an improvement scheme.
predicates.scheme_provides_shopping_sites: The scheme provides for land to be used as shopping sites.
predicates.sites_are_for_shops: The shopping sites are intended for the construction of shops.

issues.definition: In an acquisition under an improvement scheme, acquiring land for sites intended for shops is authorized when the scheme provides for those sites.

issues.legal_issue: Acquiring land for shops that serve the needs of a locality is for a public purpose even if the shops may be operated by private persons.
material_facts: The scheme provided for shops serving residents of the locality, who otherwise would have to travel to distant parts of the city to shop.
The proposed sites could be let to individuals who would build shops on them, and merchants had offered to meet acquisition costs.
The record did not establish that compensation would be paid from private individuals’ funds rather than the Board’s funds.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition was for a public purpose; the prospect of private individuals building or operating the shops did not make it an impermissible transfer of land from one private person to another.
issues.legal_principle: A purpose that directly benefits the public or a section of the public is a public purpose. Shops serving the convenience of local residents satisfy that standard. In Arnold Rodricks v. State of Maharashtra, the Court held that individual benefit from development does not displace the general public good and that development may proceed through private agencies. The record also did not support the claim that private individuals, rather than the Board, would pay compensation.

rule.if: acquisition_challenge and shops_serve_local_residents and sites_may_be_used_by_private_operators and compensation_not_shown_to_be_private

predicates.acquisition_challenge: The proceeding challenged the acquisition of land for a development scheme.
predicates.shops_serve_local_residents: The proposed shops would meet the needs and improve the convenience of residents in the locality.
predicates.sites_may_be_used_by_private_operators: The scheme allows private individuals to build or operate shops on the acquired sites.
predicates.compensation_not_shown_to_be_private: The evidence does not establish that compensation for the acquired land will be paid by private individuals rather than the acquiring public body.

issues.definition: An acquisition challenge fails on public-purpose grounds when the proposed shops serve local residents, even if private operators may use the sites, where compensation is not shown to be privately funded.
